title: Revival jazz and the missing life force
summary: Traditional New Orleans jazz, forties swing and symphony lack life force.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Or it's like traditional New Orleans jazz. It's still

there and there are still people doing it, but it's not really growing. It's lost its vitality. It's lost its life force. It's now historical, they do it because it was done before, but they don't do it with--
People aren't writing new pieces to be played by--

It doesn't have the life force and I don't know how to identify it, but that's what is lacking in each case, and it's what is lacking with forty swing too and it's something that, until you came, I thought had happened to jazz. Apparently not.
I hope not too. That's what it needs and symphony music needs the same thing. All music, all art needs that injection of needing to do it.
